Obfuscate

OB-fuh-skayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To obfuscate is to deliberately cloud, muddy, or make something unclear or confusing.

Instead of admitting the mistake, the company's statement seemed designed to obfuscate exactly what had gone wrong.

Worked Example

The contract's dense legal language seemed built to obfuscate a simple fee increase most customers would have objected to.

Obfuscate describes an intentional effort to make something unclear, usually to hide an inconvenient truth.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

cloud: make unclear or hard to understand

confuse: cause someone to become bewildered

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

clarify: make something clearer or easier to understand

illuminate: make something clear or easy to understand

Where it sits · how intentional the blurring is — confuse → obfuscate → muddy

confuse vs. obfuscate: Confuse can happen by accident; obfuscate implies an intentional effort to make something unclear.

muddy vs. obfuscate: Muddying an explanation can happen carelessly, but obfuscate more strongly implies an intentional, often self-serving motive.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ob-

prefix — ob-: toward, against (Latin)

root — fusc

root — fusc: dark (Latin (fuscus, fuscare))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: ob- ('toward') + fusc ('dark') + -ate ('to make') together mean 'to make dark' -- exactly what obfuscate does to a clear explanation.

Use the root in a new word: fuscous

Use the root in a new word: fuscous: Fuscous is a rare English color-term from the very same Latin root fuscus ('dark, dusky'), though it never became a common everyday word.
